steps.title: The rías
steps.body: Rías Baixas is in Galicia, Spain's north-west corner, on the Atlantic coast. It takes its name from the rías, flooded river valleys like fjords, that cut into the coast. Granite dominates the soils. It's green and lush, very different from the rest of Spain. The DO was created in 1988.

steps.title: Wet and mild
steps.body: The climate is maritime: mild temperatures, high humidity and lots of rain, often 1,600 mm or more a year, among Spain's wettest regions. The main challenge is fungal disease. Growers use high pergolas, parras, on granite posts, to keep grapes away from damp ground and let air flow.

steps.prompt: Why are Rías Baixas vines trained on high pergolas?
options: To let air circulate and reduce rot

steps.title: Five sub-zones
steps.body: Rías Baixas has five sub-zones. Val do Salnés, the coolest and most Atlantic, is Albariño's historic heart, around Cambados. O Rosal and Condado do Tea, along the Miño river on the Portuguese border, are warmer, and blend Albariño with Loureiro and Treixadura. Soutomaior and Ribeira do Ulla complete them.
steps.highlight: Val do Salnés, O Rosal, Condado do Tea

steps.title: What you learned
points: Rías Baixas lies on Galicia's Atlantic coast, on granite
It's wet and mild, fighting rot with high pergolas
Val do Salnés is the cool heart; the Miño zones are warmer
